title: Pointer arithmetic and valid traversal boundaries
learningObjectives: Explain the language rule and its constraints.
Trace the example and predict its behaviour.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: Pointer arithmetic is defined within an array object and one position past its final element. A one-past pointer may be compared or used as an end marker but must not be dereferenced. Pointer subtraction is defined for pointers into the same array object.
understand.whyItMatters: This knowledge helps reason about C data representation, object bounds and valid memory access.
understand.analogy: Think of memory objects as labelled storage and pointers as typed references to that storage.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal pointer, lifetime and object-access rules.

explain.narrative:
Pointer arithmetic is defined within an array object and one position past its final element. A one-past pointer may be compared or used as an end marker but must not be dereferenced. Pointer subtraction is defined for pointers into the same array object.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.code: Pointer traversal is common in low-level C, but it is safe only when pointer values stay within the same array object or its permitted one-past position.

practise.guidedTask: data + 3 points one past the last element. The loop dereferences p only while p differs from end, so the one-past pointer is never dereferenced.
practise.independentTask: Draw the three elements and mark begin and end.
hints: Rewrite the traversal using indices, then compare which version makes the bound clearer to you.
Pointer addition advances by elements, not by raw bytes.
Do not dereference the one-past pointer.
